d.g: the second largest city in Tunisia;  located in eastern Tunisia near a phosphate region

sfax.e: Borrowed from French Sfax, from Tunisian Arabic صفاقس (ṣfāqis), from Arabic صَفاقِس (ṣafāqis).

d.g: A mark that indicates that a note is to be played with a strong initial attack.

sforzando.e: Italian sforzandobor. English sforzando Borrowed from Italian sforzando.

d.g: A Neapolitan pastry made from puff pastry with a sweet filling.

sfogliatella.e: Borrowed from Italian sfogliatella, diminutive form of sfogliata, singular feminine past participial of sfogliare (“to unfold, to leaf through”), from the resemblance of the pastry's texture to the pattern of unfolding leaves.

d.g: An Arab pizza-like dish, traditionally an open-faced meat pie made with ground mutton.

sfiha.e: Borrowed from North Levantine Arabic صفيحة (ṣfīḥa), from Arabic صَفِيحَة (ṣafīḥa).

d.g: A city in Covasna County, Romania.
